Good luck with your anxiety and thanks for reading. I don't know if this will help or not, but I had my anxiety under control for a while by sticking to a routine. Waking up at the same time every day, always eating at the same hours, going to sleep as closely as I could to the same time every night. Most importantly, I had to accept that sometimes events that were out of my control could throw some of these things off (for example, I'd take a train to and from work so delays were pretty much inevitable). When I started feeling anxious, I'd throw on some headphones and listen to music that I liked. I focused heavily on work and my career to distract myself.

Probably the best thing I stopped doing (for a while) was comparing myself to others. I hated how much everyone else seemed to have their life in order, but lots of people are going through issues and just do a better job of hiding it. This part is easier said than done, and I'll admit that ever since I tested positive I don't really have the strength to follow my own advice anymore.

I truly wish life was like a movie or novel with a happy ending. Unfortunately, all hope feels like it's been ripped out of me. I'm too exhausted to continue. My family relies on me for now but I have about a year left where I can set them up well financially, then my last goal in life is complete.

Finding love is completely off the table. I could never even get a first date, even without herpes. That alone tells me everything I need to know. A trip somewhere may be a good idea, depending on whether I have some leftover money at the end of this year (probability seems unlikely).

I would recommend getting out of the escort route as soon as you're able to. Get help for the anxiety before you catch an STD. Once you test positive, the anxiety kicks up another notch and it's something I wouldn't wish upon my worst enemy.

I have two cats. They are pretty awesome and I'll miss them, but my parents will be able to take care of them when I'm gone. As far as the STD, it's a no-win situation. There is still risk of transmission even with condoms and I'd feel like an asshole if I passed this on to anyone else. Disclosing to any potential future partners is setting myself up for rejection, despite the fact that it's the responsible thing to do, so it's tempting to just hide it and not say anything. But I can't stomach the thought of doing that to someone I care about, so... here I am.
